title: Sexual vs asexual reproduction
examples: What is the main difference between these two types of reproduction?
Does asexual reproduction create variety in the offspring?
Can you give me an example of an organism that uses both methods?

explain.say: Today we will look at how living things make more life.
Sexual reproduction involves two parents creating offspring.
Asexual reproduction uses only one parent to make new life.
A key result of sexual reproduction is genetic variation in offspring.
For example, when a plant uses runners, that is asexual reproduction.
In contrast, when animals mate, they show sexual reproduction.

faq.q: Why is variation important for a species to survive?
faq.a: Variation gives some individuals traits that help them survive changes in the environment. This helps the species continue to exist over time. Students might also ask: What is natural selection? Or, How does variation help species adapt?
asks: What is the role of variation?

faq.q: Are there any animals that use asexual reproduction?
faq.a: Yes, some animals can reproduce asexually, like certain types of budding. This method is faster than waiting for a mate. Students might also ask: What is budding? Or, Can animals reproduce without mates?
asks: Is budding a form of reproduction?

faq.q: Is sexual reproduction always better than asexual reproduction?
faq.a: Neither method is always better; it depends on the situation. Sexual reproduction provides variety, which is good for long-term survival. Students might also ask: When is asexual reproduction best? Or, Are there times when one method is better?

faq.q: What is the difference between mitosis and meiosis?
faq.a: Mitosis is cell division for growth, while meiosis is for making sex cells. Meiosis is what creates the variation we see in sexual reproduction. Students might also ask: How many cells are made? Or, What is the purpose of meiosis?

faq.q: If a species reproduces asexually, will all the offspring be exactly the same?
faq.a: Yes, generally, the offspring will be genetically identical to the parent. This is because there is no mixing of genes from a second parent. Students might also ask: Are they clones? Or, Will they all be perfect copies?
asks: How similar are the babies to the parent?

facts: Sexual reproduction requires the combination of genetic material from two parents.
Asexual reproduction involves only one parent producing offspring.
Variation in offspring is a key advantage of sexual reproduction.
Some organisms use runners or budding for asexual reproduction.

quiz.say: A single bacterium dividing into two new bacteria is an example of:
quiz.why: This process involves only one parent dividing itself into identical copies.

wrong.0: Mitosis is cell division, but the term describes the process, not the reproductive type.
wrong.1: Meiosis is specifically for making sex cells, which is part of sexual reproduction.
wrong.3: This requires two different parents to combine genes.

quiz.say: When two parents combine genes to create offspring, this process is called:
quiz.why: The combination of genes from two parents is the definition of sexual reproduction.

wrong.0: Cloning describes the result (identical copies), not the reproductive method itself.
wrong.2: Budding is a specific type of asexual reproduction.
wrong.3: Fission is another type of asexual division, not involving two parents.

quiz.say: If a parent plant sends out runners that grow into new plants, this demonstrates:
quiz.why: Only one parent plant is needed to create the new, genetically similar plants.

wrong.1: Sexual reproduction requires the mixing of genes from two different parents.
wrong.2: Fertilisation is the joining of sex cells, which is part of sexual reproduction.
wrong.3: Variation is the result of sexual reproduction, not the method itself.
